comparisons.peer_summary: Provision for credit losses increased to $1.54 billion in 2024 from $1.14 billion in 2023, primarily driven by net charge-offs in the credit card portfolio.
comparisons.comparison: Both BAC and GS report on the performance of their credit card portfolios in 2024, specifically highlighting the impact of charge-offs on their provision for credit losses. BAC quantifies its credit card charge-offs as net charge-offs of $3.7 billion, an increase of $1.2 billion from the prior year, with specific attention to delinquency trends (30+ and 90+ days past due). GS reports that its total provision for credit losses was $1.54 billion, noting that this increase from 2023 primarily reflected net provisions driven by net charge-offs in the credit card portfolio. While BAC discloses the absolute dollar volume of charge-offs and delinquency balances, GS discloses the resulting expense provision driven by those charge-offs, but both identify credit card charge-offs as the primary driver of credit loss expense/provisions in 2024.
